motivation: On the earlier 24 pages, separate mean and difference heads earned 82/96 versus 79 for a direct head, but lost two net stable endpoints and missed the promotion rule. That sample included just three neutral endpoints. This independent development experiment covers natural neutral transitions and existing stable claims.
hypothesis: Given two normalized layer-16 Qwen verdict representations, separately estimating the unordered pair of labels and its orientation improves factual verdicts over a direct linear readout or a simple paired mean/difference readout. Swapping evidence editions must swap both outputs. No previous gold label is available at inference.
sample: 240 calibration pages from the publisher training split; 44 other pages from its development split. One claim, two real evidence editions per page, both viewing directions. The fixed stratified sample deliberately includes changed and stable labels. All 184 pages fitted, inspected or reserved in the previous experiment are excluded.
features_and_methods: One fixed ridge penalty fraction 0.05. Even features are the mean state and absolute half-difference, standardized by training block RMS. Estimate six unordered label-pair probabilities and a signed orientation separately, then marginalize to the two endpoint labels. Compare exact full, old, full contrast, explicit two-passage prompt, supervised direct and mean/difference Qwen heads; two published ALBERT checkpoints and the same three trained heads on each model's logits.
keep: Advance if structured Qwen gives at least four more correct endpoints out of 88 than the strongest comparator, and at most one net stable endpoint lost versus the direct Qwen head. Otherwise retain development evidence only. No official test split or reserved confirmation page is opened. End-to-end timing must be measured separately if promoted.
budget: Local Apple M5 only. 1200 seconds per Qwen split, 900 per specialist split. No GPUtw or Adaption charge.
